questions.scenario: Your friend group is panicking one day before the final exams. You all meet up for a group study session. What is your role?

options.A: Standing up in front of everyone, acting like a teacher, and energetically explaining the concepts so they don't fall asleep.
options.B: Going through the previous year question papers (PYQs) to predict exactly which 5-mark questions the teacher will ask.
options.C: Drawing super neat, color-coded mind maps and diagrams so everyone can easily visualize and memorize the chapter.
options.D: Making the timetable: 'Okay guys, 45 minutes of Physics, a 10-minute Maggi break, and then we attack Chemistry.'

questions.scenario: You decide to start a 'Study Vlog' for YouTube or Instagram. What is the most important part of the video for you?

options.A: Talking directly to the camera, giving out motivational quotes or 'shayari' to keep other students pumped up.
options.B: Listing out the exact chapter weightage, syllabus breakdowns, and which reference books are actually useful.
options.C: Adding aesthetic lofi beats, cool text pop-ups, and smooth transitions to make the vlog look cinematic.
options.D: Checking the analytics to see which hashtags to use and exactly what time to post so it gets maximum views.

questions.scenario: The teacher assigns a group presentation on 'The Human Heart' or 'World War II'. How do you contribute?

options.A: You immediately volunteer to do all the talking on stage. You love holding the mic and keeping the class entertained.
options.B: You read the NCERT line-by-line to ensure all the dates, hardcore facts, and definitions are 100% accurate.
options.C: You spend hours on Canva finding the perfect GIFs, fonts, and layouts to make the slides look absolutely stunning.
options.D: You divide the work among your friends, set a strict deadline, and make sure everything is combined before the final bell.

questions.scenario: Your favorite EdTech bhaiya/didi launches a massive new 'Crash Course' live stream. What catches your attention the most?

options.A: Their high energy and how they aggressively motivate the chat with 'Aag laga denge!' vibes.
options.B: The description box, because you immediately want to download the PDF of the Daily Practice Problems (DPPs).
options.C: The smartboard graphics, especially the cool 3D animations they use to explain tough physics concepts.
options.D: How smartly they promoted their new paid test series right in the middle of the free video without making it boring.

questions.scenario: You are participating in an inter-school debate competition. What is your preparation strategy?

options.A: Practicing your voice modulation, hand gestures, and dramatic pauses in front of the mirror.
options.B: Digging deep into articles and data to find solid facts that will destroy the opponent's arguments.
options.C: Designing a very striking chart paper or prop to hold up while speaking to visually grab the judges' attention.
options.D: Organizing the team, coordinating practice timings, and deciding which speaker goes first for maximum impact.

questions.scenario: You are trying to solve a really tough, brain-twisting problem from R.D. Sharma or H.C. Verma. How do you handle it?

options.A: Once you crack it, you excitedly turn to your benchmate and teach them the shortcut trick you just discovered.
options.B: You analyze the step-by-step logic and check if it matches the pattern of questions usually asked in board exams.
options.C: You draw a quick, detailed sketch of the pulleys, blocks, or geometry in the margins to actually 'see' the problem.
options.D: You calculate how much time this one question is taking and decide to skip it for now to maximize your overall score.

questions.scenario: It's time to plan the farewell party for the 12th standard seniors! What is your main job?

options.A: Grabbing the mic! You want to host the event, roast the seniors, and make everyone laugh out loud.
options.B: Creating the trivia quiz for the seniors, making sure the questions are nostalgic but surprisingly tricky.
options.C: Editing the farewell video montage with old photos, funny clips, and emotional Bollywood music.
options.D: Managing the chanda (money collection), negotiating with the DJ, and making sure the samosas arrive hot and on time.

questions.scenario: During a free period, the teacher is absent and the class is getting loud and bored. What do you do?

options.A: Go to the front and start mimicking your strict teachers or doing a mini stand-up comedy routine.
options.B: Start asking your friends tricky riddles or puzzles to see who has the smartest brain in the group.
options.C: Start doodling crazy caricatures of your friends or sketching a comic strip on the back page of your notebook.
options.D: Invent a new game using just a pen and paper, establish the rules, and organize a mini-tournament for the backbenchers.

questions.scenario: Your parents force you to help your younger sibling with their daily homework. What is your teaching style?

options.A: Making them repeat the answers loudly with you until they memorize it with full energy.
options.B: Creating a surprise mini mock-test on a rough copy to check if they *actually* understood it, or just memorized it.
options.C: Using their sketch pens to draw colorful diagrams so the boring textbook suddenly looks interesting.
options.D: Setting a timer and offering a deal: 'Finish this in 20 minutes, and I'll let you play games on my phone.'

questions.scenario: You notice your school's official magazine is super boring. If you could change one thing, what would it be?

options.A: Writing a fiery, motivational editorial piece on the first page to totally hype up the students.
options.B: Adding a highly detailed section on 'How to crack competitive exams' with expert book recommendations.
options.C: Completely redesigning the cover page and layout so it looks modern, vibrant, and visually stunning.
options.D: Campaigning to increase the magazine's popularity by convincing the principal to add a 'Student of the Month' prize.

Role_1.title: Star On-Camera Educator
Role_1.primary_match_text: You are the charismatic face of learning! You have the energy, the voice, and the magnetic personality to make even the most boring topics sound like blockbuster movies. You know how to connect with an audience and keep them hooked.
Role_1.day_in_the_life: Standing in front of a smartboard, cracking relatable jokes, breaking down tough concepts, and motivating lakhs of students on live streams and YouTube videos.
Role_1.alternative_match_text: Your high energy and communication skills also make you a perfect fit for Public Speaking, TV Anchoring, or becoming a Motivational Coach.
Role_1.educational_roadmap: Choose any stream you love in 11th/12th. Pursue a degree in your subject of interest (B.Tech, B.Sc, or BA). The key is mastering your subject and practicing public speaking. Getting a B.Ed can also give you a solid foundation in teaching methodologies.

Role_2.title: Curriculum & Assessment Designer
Role_2.primary_match_text: You are the mastermind behind the scenes! You love finding patterns, designing the perfect syllabus, and creating those brain-teasing questions that test real knowledge. You ensure the content is top-quality.
Role_2.day_in_the_life: Analyzing past years' JEE/NEET/Board papers, structuring study modules, creating tricky MCQs, and ensuring the educational content is 100% error-free and up-to-date with NCERT guidelines.
Role_2.alternative_match_text: Your sharp analytical brain and attention to detail also make you a great fit for Academic Research, Data Analysis, or Book Publishing.
Role_2.educational_roadmap: Take Science or Commerce in 11th/12th. Pursue an undergraduate degree in your specialized subject (e.g., B.Sc, B.Tech, BA Economics). A Master's degree (M.Sc/MA) or a B.Ed often helps you become an expert in building educational frameworks.

Role_3.title: Video Editor & Animator
Role_3.primary_match_text: You are the visual magician! You know exactly how to use colors, transitions, and effects to grab someone's attention. You can take a complex, boring concept and explain it beautifully using visuals.
Role_3.day_in_the_life: Taking raw teaching footage, cutting out the boring parts, adding cool 3D animations of the human heart or physics gravity models, and designing click-worthy thumbnails that students can't resist.
Role_3.alternative_match_text: Your strong creative vision also makes you perfect for Graphic Design, Film Editing, UI/UX Design, or Advertising.
Role_3.educational_roadmap: Any stream in 11th/12th works! Pursue a B.Sc in Animation & VFX, BA in Mass Communication, or a specialized diploma in Multimedia & Video Editing. Building a strong portfolio of your edits is the most important step!

Role_4.title: EdTech Channel Head / Course Manager
Role_4.primary_match_text: You are the strategic boss! You understand how things work, how to organize people, and how to turn a good idea into a massive success. You love seeing the big picture and leading the team to victory.
Role_4.day_in_the_life: Looking at YouTube analytics, deciding when to launch a new 'Crash Course' batch, managing the budget, and coordinating between teachers and editors to ensure everything releases on time.
Role_4.alternative_match_text: Your leadership and organizational skills make you a fantastic fit for Product Management, Digital Marketing, or even founding your own Startup.
Role_4.educational_roadmap: Commerce or any stream in 11th/12th. Pursue a BBA, B.Com, or B.Tech. Follow it up with an MBA in Marketing, Operations, or EdTech Management from a top Indian institute to master the business side of education.
